title: Earth's magnetic poles have flipped hundreds of times
body: Cooling lava freezes in the direction of the field, and ocean-floor stripes record the geomagnetic polarity flipping irregularly, on average every few hundred thousand years. During a reversal, taking thousands of years, the field weakens and wanders into multiple poles. Compasses in such eras would be unreliable narrators. The last full flip was about 780,000 years ago.
